correctness.rationale: For the smooth plane quartic, the exact Cech/Frobenius coefficient identity gives the Hasse--Witt matrix with sole off-diagonal coefficients 3b(a²+b) and 1. Smoothness is b(a²+b) ≠ 0. Frobenius squared is diag(0,c,c^5) with c ≠ 0, proving stable rank two, a-number one, and Newton slopes (0,0,1/2,1/2,1,1). The tame genus-one quotient is j=0 and supersingular in characteristic five, so the Prym is ordinary by the prime-to-five isogeny. The bundled exact symbolic checker confirms the critical matrix; finite-field counts are corroboration only.

originality.rationale: The inspected directly related publications identify the bielliptic Picard family and Prym (2023/2025) and a special Fermat-type member (2015), but do not establish that all smooth characteristic-five members have stable Frobenius rank two and ordinary Pryms. The fixed-parameter result of 2015 is strictly weaker. The 1991 abstract promises general extreme-rank Hasse--Witt criteria; a potentially dominating general formula remains a specific historical residual risk, explicitly disclosed.
residual_risks: Estrada-Sarlabous (1991) may contain general Hasse--Witt formulas from which the uniform characteristic-five identity follows; full text could not be inspected.
Published general Picard-curve Cartier--Manin algorithms or small-prime tables may subsume the result despite no equivalent explicit family statement identified.
The more recent same-family study contains substantial geometry and isogeny structure but does not, in the inspected sections, assert the present mod-five constant Newton polygon.

value.rationale: A complete nonordinary characteristic-five Newton stratum for the entire natural one-dimensional bielliptic Picard family, together with ordinarity of its Prym locus, determines a geometric and arithmetic invariant of an existing moduli family. The fact that the single characteristic-five Fermat member has p-rank two does not imply this rigidity, and the smoothness discriminant nonvanishing being exactly the Frobenius-rank factor is a meaningful geometric compatibility, not an arbitrary numerical slice.
